bf.reason: Bond Forge drops its own flex-column/gap stack and left alignment: the shared title/status/username-row margins already space the standard block flow, and the leaderboard text alignment follows the result card like every other page.
The standard leaderboard title is sentence case on every page; Bond Forge no longer upper-cases it.
The standard list shows the platform scrollbar on every page; Bond Forge no longer hides it, so overflow past the shared max-height stays discoverable.
Standard rows centre rank/name/score vertically; Bond Forge used baseline alignment only because its rows had no padding.
Bond Forge spelled the fixed rank column as flex: 0 0 22px; the shared rule expresses the same 22px non-shrinking column as width + flex-shrink.

Bond Forge intentionally gives up its non-shrinking score column (flex: 0 0 auto, i.e. flex-shrink: 0); the score now uses the default flex-shrink: 1 like every other page, next to the shared flex: 1 / min-width: 0 name that absorbs overflow first.
flex: 0 0 auto and the shared flex-shrink: 0 both keep the label at its content width.
The shared input already removes the UA outline (its :focus rule restyles the border instead); Bond Forge did the same in its own :focus rule.
